ja: 今週末、埋め合わせさせてもらえませんか？
en: Can I make it up to you this weekend?
alternatives: Could I make it up to you this weekend?
Can I make it up to you over the weekend?
point: 埋め合わせる は make it up to 人

ja: ミスに気づいてくれてありがとう。
en: Thanks for catching the mistake.
alternatives: Thank you for spotting the mistake.
Thanks for noticing the error.
point: Thanks for の後は動詞の ing 形

ja: 車で送ってもらわなきゃ、面接に間に合わなかった。
en: If you hadn't driven me, I'd have missed the interview.
alternatives: Without your ride, I'd have missed the interview.
I would've missed the interview if you hadn't driven me.
point: 過去の仮定は had 過去分詞、帰結は would have 過去分詞

ja: 資料をまだお返ししておらず、すみません。
en: I'm sorry I still haven't returned your documents.
alternatives: Sorry I haven't returned your documents yet.
I apologize, I haven't returned your documents yet.
point: 「まだ〜していない」は still haven't returned

ja: 送る前に確認すべきでした。すみません。
en: Sorry, I should've checked before sending it.
alternatives: Sorry, I should have double-checked it first.
I should have checked it before sending. Sorry.
point: 「〜すべきだった」は should have + 過去分詞

ja: 田中くんが気づかなきゃ、数字を間違えて送ってた。
en: If Tanaka hadn't noticed, we'd have sent the wrong numbers.
alternatives: Had Tanaka not noticed, we'd have sent the wrong numbers.
If Tanaka hadn't noticed, I'd have sent the wrong numbers.
point: 過去の事実の裏は If S had done, S would have done

ja: 彼女の誕生会を欠席したこと、謝ればよかった。
en: I wish I'd apologized for missing her party.
alternatives: If only I'd apologized for missing her party.
I wish I had said sorry for missing her party.
I should have apologized for missing her party.
point: 過去への後悔は wish の後を過去完了にする

ja: 私のミスだ。私が謝るべきだよ。
en: My mistake. I should apologize.
alternatives: It was my mistake. I should apologize.
I should apologize. It was my mistake.
point: should の後ろは動詞の原形 apologize

ja: 私のせいで皆に週末出勤させて、ごめん。
en: Sorry I made everyone work this weekend.
alternatives: I'm sorry I made everyone work this weekend.
Sorry I made you all work this weekend.
point: make + 人 + 動詞の原形。to は付けない

ja: 君がいなきゃ、まだ報告書で詰まってたよ。
en: Without you, I'd still be stuck on this report.
alternatives: If it weren't for you, I'd still be stuck.
I'd still be struggling with this report without you.
point: 今も続く状況の仮定は I'd still be で表す

ja: 近所を案内してもらえたのが、何より嬉しかった。
en: What meant the most to me was you showing me around.
alternatives: What I appreciated most was you showing me around the neighborhood.
Nothing meant more to me than you showing me around.
point: 「何より嬉しかったこと」を主語にして was で受ける

ja: ありがとう。一週間ずっと詰まってたんだ。
en: Thanks. I've been stuck all week.
alternatives: Thanks. I've been stuck for a week.
Thank you. I've been struggling all week.
point: 今も続く状態は I've been ~ で表す

ja: 私のミスです。次は確認します。
en: My mistake. I'll double-check next time.
alternatives: That's my fault. I'll check next time.
My mistake. I'll check next time.
point: その場で決めた約束は will を使う

ja: 残業してくれた先輩に、ランチをおごった。
en: I bought my coworker lunch for staying late.
alternatives: I treated my coworker to lunch for staying late.
I bought my coworker lunch for working late.
point: 「おごる」は buy 人 lunch / treat 人 to lunch、理由は for + -ing

ja: 君の誕生日を忘れてごめん。
en: Sorry, I forgot your birthday.
alternatives: I'm sorry I forgot your birthday.
I forgot your birthday. I'm sorry.
point: 「忘れた」は過去形。forget は forgot と不規則に変わる

ja: ご注文が違う住所に送られてしまいました。
en: Your order was sent to the wrong address.
alternatives: Your order was shipped to the wrong address.
Your order got sent to the wrong address.
point: 「送られた」は was sent、住所は the wrong address

ja: 昨日は電話に出られなくてごめん。
en: Sorry I couldn't answer your call yesterday.
alternatives: Sorry I couldn't take your call yesterday.
Sorry I couldn't pick up yesterday.
point: 過去の「できなかった」は couldn't で表す

ja: ありがとう。君は優しいね。
en: Thanks. You're so kind.
alternatives: Thank you. You're very kind.
Thanks a lot. You're really kind.
point: 「優しい」は be 動詞＋kind。You kind としない

ja: 問題を起こしたのは、チームではなく私の確認不足でした。
en: It was my oversight, not the team's, that caused the problem.
alternatives: What caused the problem was my oversight, not the team's.
The team wasn't to blame; my oversight caused the problem.
point: It was A, not B, that で「B ではなく A が」を強調

ja: うちのせいじゃないのに、課長は謝った。
en: Even though it wasn't our fault, my manager apologized.
alternatives: My manager apologized even though it wasn't our fault.
Although it wasn't our fault, my manager still apologized.
It wasn't our fault, but my manager apologized anyway.
point: 「〜のに」は even though で対比させる
